I couldn't find a direct, comprehensive list of steps for non-payment of rent in a general context in the Acts I searched, but the sources provide specific provisions regarding rent defaults, ejectment, and protection against eviction in certain jurisdictions and under specific statutes.

Under Section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a landlord may apply to the Controller for an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of the rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him [2]. However, no order for recovery of possession on this ground shall be made if the tenant makes payment or deposit as required by section 15 [2].

rows.question: police meri FIR darj nahi kar rahi, ab kya karu
queries: police meri FIR darj nahi kar rahi, ab kya karu

topSources: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 s173

rows.answer:
If the police refuse to record your information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, you may send the substance of such information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police concerned under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [1]. If the Superintendent of Police is satisfied that the information discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, he shall either investigate the case himself or direct an investigation to be made by a subordinate police officer [1]. If the police still do not record the information, the aggrieved person may make an application to the Magistrate under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [1].

rows.question: Does the limitation period apply to arbitration, and how long do I have to file a suit for a loan I gave?
queries: Does the limitation period apply to arbitration, and how long do I have to file a suit for a loan I gave?
limitation period applicability to arbitration proceedings
limitation period for recovery of loan suit for money lent
Limitation Act section 21 arbitration limitation period and section 19 loan recovery
topSources: The Limitation Act, 1963 s21
The Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 s43
The Limitation Act, 1963 sA19
The Limitation Act, 1963 sA21
The Limitation Act, 1963 sA20
rows.answer:
The limitation period applies to arbitration [2][6][7]. The period of limitation for any dispute required to be referred to arbitration shall be regulated by the provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963, as if the dispute were a suit and the arbitrator a civil court, though an arbitrator may admit a dispute after the expiry of the period of limitation if the applicant satisfies the arbitrator of sufficient cause for not referring the dispute within such period [2][6][7]. Under Section 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to arbitrations as it applies to proceedings in court, and an arbitration is deemed to have commenced on the date referred to in Section 21 [7].

For a suit for money lent, the limitation period depends on the nature of the agreement as provided in the First Division, Part II of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963:
- For money payable for money lent, the period of limitation is three years from when the loan is made, under Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [3].

rows.question: IPC 420 cheating punishment
queries: IPC 420 cheating punishment
cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property punishment IPC 420
IPC section 420
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita section 318 cheating
topSources: The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860 (Rep., Act 45 of 2023) s420
The INDIAN PENAL CODE s420
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 s318
EDMUNDS LYNGDOH versus STATE OF MEGHALAYA s?
RAM NARAIN POPLI versus CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION s?
rows.answer:
The punishment for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and liability to a fine, under Section 420 of The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860 [1] and Section 420 of The INDIAN PENAL CODE (chandigarh) [2]. The same punishment applies under Section 318(4) of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [3].

Related provisions:
- Section 318(1) of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers cheating by deceiving any person and fraudulently or dishonestly inducing delivery of property, consent to retain property, or intentional inducement to do or omit anything causing damage or harm [3].
- Section 318(2) of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers general cheating punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both [3].
- Section 318(3) of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which covers cheating with the knowledge that it is likely to cause wrongful loss to a person whose interest the offender was bound by law or legal contract to protect, punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or with fine, or with both [3].
